title: Rolling probe calibration: traffic-shape-aware SLO thresholds and Terraform-managed probe configs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Existing VPC health probes and SLO alerts are calibrated to static thresholds which cause noisy alerts during traffic shape changes (batch windows, nightly spikes) and after runtime upgrades. This ticket implements a rolling calibration system that 1) derives adaptive SLO thresholds from recent traffic shape and latency baselines, 2) persists probe configuration via Terraform-managed parameters so upgrades are reproducible and auditable, and 3) provides a safe canary/rollback path for recalibration during Private (VPC) upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Adaptive servo computes per-pool 95th and 99th latency baselines over sliding 1h/24h windows and exposes calibrated thresholds to probe controller
Terraform module (modules/vpc_probe_config) manages probe definitions and publishes config to SSM/Consul (customer option) with version tags

Canary recalibration rollout that updates 10% of nodes first, validates synthetic probe pass rate and token throughput stability for 30 minutes, auto-rolls back if error-rate delta > 0.5% or token throughput drops > 15%
Alerting rule changes reduce alert flapping: minimum evaluation window 3m with 2 consecutive breaches required before paging
Telemetry dashboards show latency percentile drift and calibration delta for each VPC pool; historical calibration versions are queryable
Automated integration test that injects synthetic traffic patterns (spiky, steady, ramp) and asserts thresholds adapt within expected bounds without generating a paging alert
plan: Design adaptive calibration algorithm (token-bucket based smoothing + percentile extrapolation)
Implement probe controller changes to accept dynamic thresholds and gracefully reload without dropping in-flight requests
Add Terraform module to manage probe config artifacts and tie versions to release tags
Build canary orchestration: controller flags, rollout percentages, and health gates wired into existing deployment pipeline
Update alerting/playbooks and add a dashboard for calibration observability
Run staged validation in staging -> private-edge -> customer-simulated environments, then schedule private-region rollouts
tradeoffs: Adaptive thresholds reduce noise but risk masking regressions if the calibration window is too large; chosen windows (1h/24h) balance responsiveness vs stability
Persisting configs in Terraform increases operational rigor and auditability but requires a migration for existing ad-hoc configs; migration path is included in the module
Canary windows add rollout latency; we prefer a conservative canary to avoid customer-impacting regressions in Private deployments
More aggressive rollback thresholds decrease blast radius but may trigger false rollbacks in noisy environments; tuned thresholds were validated against six weeks of historical telemetry
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Lab): unit tests + local simulation of traffic shapes
Phase 1 (Staging): deploy probe controller + Terraform module to staging VPCs; run synthetic patterns for 48h
Phase 2 (Private Edge Canary): enable calibrated probes on 10% of private-edge workers using canary orchestration; monitor for 30-60m
Phase 3 (Gradual): 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 2h observation between steps unless a gate fires
Phase 4 (Customers): opt-in for tenant-level config; for managed customers schedule maintenance windows and provide upgrade playbook
test_plan: Unit tests for calibration math and percentiles (95/99) using synthetic traces
Integration test: controller reload with zero-downtime on config change
Load test: token throughput baseline verification under steady and burst traffic for each canary step
Chaos test: simulate KV cache thrash and ensure calibration does not mask genuine regressions
E2E: Terraform apply/destroy cycle for modules/vpc_probe_config and a migration run for a sample existing config
